title: Quotient criterion for the scalar-extension unit of an ideal subsheaf
statement: Let R,B be commutative ring sheaves on a small site, phi:R -> B, and I an ideal subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal]. If I.IsQuotientIso phi holds, the unit of the sheafified scalar-extension adjunction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus] is invertible on the categorical cokernel of I.inclusion. Flatness and finite generation are not required.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03CY; the quotient hypothesis used in Algebraization Tag 099I

proof.text: Construct the sectionwise quotient presheaves, their projections, and their coefficient comparison. The kernel and lifting clauses of IsQuotientIso give injectivity and local surjectivity. Sheafification turns the comparison into an isomorphism; the explicit sheafified quotient cofork identifies it with the coefficient map on categorical cokernels.

Construct the scalar extension of the ring module and its inverse using the scalar-extension adjunction and the unit-section equivalence. Construct the map from the extended source ideal to the target ideal. Every local finite sum of target coefficients times source ideal sections lifts through this map, so it is epic.

Scalar extension preserves cokernels. The epic ideal map and the ring-module isomorphism identify the extended source quotient with the target quotient. Check after the quotient projection that its composite with the adjunction unit is the coefficient quotient comparison. Cancel the target isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03D7 and 03CY; the quotient hypothesis used in Algebraization Tag 099I
